statement: Inferact reports a TPU v7 Ironwood megakernel serving Moonshot AI Kimi K3 at 700 tokens/s with speculative decoding on 16 chips, versus 452 tokens/s on 16 Nvidia GB200 GPUs running standard vLLM, a 1.57x advantage.
why: A non-Nvidia inference path showing parity-or-better decode throughput weakens the assumption that merchant GPUs are the only viable platform for serving frontier-scale models.

impact.mechanism: If TPU-class accelerators plus a fused single-program decode kernel match or beat GB200 throughput on real models, inference buyers can substitute hyperscaler ASIC capacity for merchant GPU capacity, and software fusion becomes a lever on effective capacity.

evidence.excerpt: the TPU v7 Ironwood megakernel achieved 700 tokens/s (reported elsewhere as 709 tokens/s) versus 452 tokens/s on GB200 in the standard vLLM configuration
Without speculative decoding, at batch size 1, the megakernel achieved 249 tokens/s versus 127 tokens/s on the GPU baseline

confidence.basis: Single secondary vendor blog post; the benchmark is self-reported by the party promoting the technique and covers one model on one configuration.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 1 -> 2; sources: Inferact
entity: Google TPU v7 Ironwood, Nvidia GB200, Moonshot AI Kimi K3, Inferact
